stem: Calcium and its compounds have a large variety of applications.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: Calcium metal reacts readily with most acids.
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of calcium with dilute nitric acid. State symbols are not required.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text:
When calcium metal is placed in dilute sulfuric acid, it reacts vigorously at first.

After a short time, a crust of calcium sulfate forms on the calcium metal and the reaction stops. Some of the calcium metal and dilute sulfuric acid remain unreacted.

Suggest an explanation for these observations.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: Calcium ethanedioate is formed when calcium reacts with ethanedioic acid, $(\text{CO}_2\text{H})_2$. The compound contains one cation and one anion.
parts.text: Draw the 'dot-and-cross' diagram of the cation present in calcium ethanedioate. Show all electrons.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the displayed formula of the anion present in calcium ethanedioate.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Calcium chlorate(I), $\text{Ca}(\text{ClO})_2$, is used as an alternative to sodium chlorate(I), $\text{NaClO}$, in some household products.
parts.text: Suggest a use for calcium chlorate(I).

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The chlorate(I) ion is formed when cold aqueous sodium hydroxide reacts with chlorine.

Write an ionic equation for this reaction. State symbols are not required.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
(c)(iv)
parts.text: In terms of electron transfer, state what happens to the chlorine in the reaction in (iii).

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
Calcium lactate is used in some medicines. It forms when lactic acid (2-hydroxypropanoic acid) reacts with calcium carbonate.

{{figure:pdf_visual_02.png}}
parts.text: Identify the two other products of the reaction of lactic acid with calcium carbonate.

Lactic acid has a chiral centre.

State what is meant by the term chiral centre.
